objective: Diagnose a NOT IN filter that returns nothing because the list contains a NULL, and fix it with NOT EXISTS

sources.cite: PostgreSQL 16 documentation, 9.23 Subquery Expressions (9.23.3 NOT IN)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16 (PostgreSQL 16.16 documentation). Relevant text: 'Note that if the left-hand expression yields null, or if there are no equal right-hand values and at least one right-hand row yields null, the result of the NOT IN construct will be null, not true. This is in accordance with SQL's normal rules for Boolean combinations of null values.' The page documents EXISTS (9.23.1); NOT EXISTS is its negation, and the summary did not quote a NOT EXISTS paragraph. A WHERE clause keeps only rows whose condition is true, so a null NOT IN drops every row.

brief.situation: You are the analyst at Maple & Pine Home Goods (fictional). Marketing wants every customer who has not ordered since 1 October for a win-back mailing that goes to the printer at 12:00. Your usual query, which worked last quarter, returns no rows. Guest checkout went live in September. It is 11:15.
handover: Guest checkout stores an order without a customer_id.

writeup.question: For the analytics channel: why the query returned nothing, what you changed, and how you know the list is complete.

parts.label: Why nothing came back
parts.criteria: The subquery's list contains NULLs (guest orders); for a customer not in the list, NOT IN compares with NULL and is unknown, never true, so WHERE keeps no row.
parts.modelAnswer: 212 guest orders have customer_id NULL; x NOT IN (..., NULL) is null when x matches nothing, so every row is dropped.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery (or NOT IN over non-NULL values); no data changed; not a LEFT JOIN with the date filter in WHERE.
parts.modelAnswer: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.ordered_at >= DATE '2026-10-01').

scoring.modelReasoning: If the subquery returns a NULL, then for a customer that matches nothing, customer_id NOT IN (...) is null rather than true, and WHERE keeps only true rows, so the query returns nothing. Guest checkout put 212 NULL customer_ids in this quarter's orders. NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery is true exactly when no matching order exists; NOT IN over non-NULL values also works. A LEFT JOIN with the date filter in WHERE discards the unmatched rows it was meant to find, and deleting guest orders destroys real sales. An independent count (18,240 - 15,911 = 2,329) proves the list complete.
